The house standard requires every 'X likely' to be a probable rule; the two inflammatory features that are checked for are only ever used as negations. text: Both rules diagnose the identical concept 'Acute pyelonephritis' probable, and the uncomplicated rule's evidence is a strict subset of the complicated rule's, so every complicated case also satisfies the uncomplicated rule and the system cannot tell the page's two outcomes apart. The uncomplicated rule should at least carry (no ...) for the complicating factors, and the shared concept should be recorded as a SNOMED gap.

Fever is negated as (no (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Fever" "finding"))) whereas the house convention and the TB rule in the same file use (active_condition (snomed_concept "Fever" "finding")). If fever is recorded as an active condition the negation may not see it, so a febrile patient can be diagnosed with mechanical back pain while also being flagged as possible TB.

Age criteria ('> 50 years' and '< 40 years') are not representable in the grammar, so two of the page's branch conditions are silently absent from the rule. This is a language limitation but it is not flagged anywhere in the file and the rule fires for patients the page would route to a doctor.
